title: How to Find the Australia Median Salary and Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your annual pay from an hourly rate, understand the australia median salary, and see the National Minimum Wage, tax, and super for 2026–27.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: What is the australia median salary?
faqs.a: The australia median salary is not a single figure published by the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The ABS provides average weekly earnings, which differ from the median. For a typical salary in your occupation, check your award or industry pay guide.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours (commonly 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 gross per year. The timesheet on this site does this for you.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include super and tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The calculator estimates gross annual pay, then adds superannuation at 12% on top (up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base) and deducts tax using the 2026–27 resident rates plus the Medicare levy. It is an estimate only and does not include HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to convert it to an annual figure. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. This gives you your gross annual pay before tax and super.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparing offers or understanding your earning potential.

While the Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings, the **australia median salary** is a different measure that reflects the middle point of all salaries. The ABS does not release a single median figure for the whole country; instead, they provide averages. For a more tailored view, refer to industry awards or the [pay guides](/blog) on this site.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making their minimum **$33.05 per hour**. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave.

Award rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. They apply to specific industries and occupations and include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay is set by that award, not the national minimum. Use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page to see current rates, and check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

Casual loading is an additional 25% on the base hourly rate. It is not included in the base rate you enter into the timesheet. Instead, you tick a checkbox to add it on top. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For more details, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

## Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the National Minimum Wage example: $1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. If you are paid weekly, your gross pay is the weekly figure.

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your hourly rate and see your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay instantly. It also handles the casual loading checkbox so you don’t have to calculate it manually.

## Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution to your super fund.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more detail on after-tax amounts.

## Average vs Median Pay

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes **Average Weekly Earnings** for full-time adult ordinary time: **$2,083.70 per week** (May 2026). For all employees (including part-time), the average is **$1,579.20 per week**. These are averages, not medians. The **australia median salary** is a different statistic that is not directly provided by the ABS. Median pay is often lower than the average because high earners pull the average up. For a better idea of typical pay in your role, consult industry awards or the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) reference tables.

## Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/) is the home page of this site. You type your base hourly rate into the input field. If you are a casual employee, tick the “Add 25% casual loading” checkbox. The calculator then adds the loading on top of your base rate. It does not expect you to enter a rate that already includes loading. The results show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated super and tax.

For more on converting hourly rates, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion). If you want to compare pay across jobs, the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page offers guidance.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
